title: {Syn} Euclid Still Wins the Prime Game
content:
Euclid proved that there are infinitely many primes more than two thousand years ago. The trick is still beautifully compact: multiply any finite list of primes, add 1, and the result has a prime divisor that was not in the original list.

The proof does not give the next prime efficiently, but it shows why a complete prime catalog can never exist. That gap between existence and efficient discovery is a recurring theme in number theory.

Why it matters: number theory keeps producing ideas that are simple enough to state and strong enough to build with.
